compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Task

Create `plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh` — the migration script that appends an empty `## Closure Checks` section to all epic/story tickets that lack it.

## Testing Mode: RED

This task makes the T1 RED test turn GREEN. Do NOT write or modify the test in this task.

## File Impact
- `plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh` (create, must chmod +x)

## Implementation (Approach A — mirrors ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh)

### Interface

```
migrate-closure-checks.sh [--target <host-project-root>] [--dry-run] [--resume <progress-file>] [--ticket-list <file>]
```

Flags:
- `--target <path>`: host project root (default: git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
- `--dry-run`: read-only mode; prints DRY-RUN:<id> lines, writes no events, no stamp file
- `--resume <progress-file>`: skip ticket IDs listed in the progress JSON file
- `--ticket-list <file>`: one ticket ID per line; if absent, auto-discovers all epic/story tickets missing the section

Exit codes: 0 = success (including idempotent re-run), 1 = fatal error

### Sentinel / Idempotency
- Global stamp file: `<target>/.claude/.closure-checks-migration-v1`
- Per-ticket: skip if existing ticket description already contains `## Closure Checks`
- On re-run with stamp file present: emit SKIPPED:<id>:already-has-section for all and exit 0

### Core logic (Python inline heredoc)

Single-pass Python scan over the tracker directory:
1. For each ticket in tracker: read all event files (sorted by name for timestamp order)
2. Reconstruct current description from CREATE + EDIT events (latest EDIT wins)
3. If description already contains `## Closure Checks`: emit SKIPPED:<id>:already-has-section
4. Otherwise: compute new description by appending `\n\n## Closure Checks\n\n_No closure checks defined yet._` after the last line of `## Success Criteria` section (or at end of description if no SC section)
5. Emit WROTE:<id>:<event_filename> for bash to git-commit

### Batch semantics
- Process in batches of 25 tickets
- After each batch, emit: BATCH_COMPLETE:<batch_num>:<processed_this_batch>:<total_processed>:<grand_total>
- Update progress JSON file at `/tmp/closure-migration-progress-<session_timestamp>.json` after each batch

### Progress / Resume
- Progress file (mktemp-generated path, printed to stdout at start): JSON object {"migrated": [<id>, ...], "skipped": [<id>, ...], "session_start": <timestamp>}
- On `--resume <file>`: load progress file, union of migrated+skipped = already-done set; skip those IDs

### Git commits
Bash loop commits each WROTE:<id>:<fname> immediately:
```bash
git -C "" add "<id>/<fname>" && git -C "" commit -m "migration: add ## Closure Checks scaffold to <id>"
```

### Plugin-source-repo guard
Exit 0 with NOTICE if `<target>/plugin.json` exists (same guard as ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh)

### Help output
`--help` prints usage including restart procedure for --resume

## Acceptance Criteria
- `bash tests/scripts/test-migrate-closure-checks.sh` produces PASSED: N FAILED: 0
- Script is executable: `test -x plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh`
- Running script on a tracker where all tickets already have the section exits 0 with all SKIPPED lines
- DRY-RUN mode makes no file changes and writes no stamp file
- Re-running after stamp file exists is idempotent (exits 0, all SKIPPED)
